A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same NuPlanQA work, with corresponding sections, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices or the supplementary material mentioned in the text; the comparison covers all supplied content.

before.justification: v1 reports original NuPlanQA-Eval model evaluations in Table 2 and BEV-Fusion and input-type ablations in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original evaluations and ablations, with revised comparison-model results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The BEV-LLM architecture, temporal self-attention, BEV-to-visual fusion, multimodal projector, and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2.4 and 3.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use NuPlanQA-1M and NuPlanQA-Eval with the same nine driving subtasks, four-city source coverage, and single/multiple-view and frame scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same two commercial and six open-source comparators under both frame conditions. Table 3 retains the same baseline and BEV-Fusion variants; only Table 2 scores change.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly specifies zero-shot evaluation in v1 but deletes that statement in v2 without describing a replacement setting. Splits, input formats, model sizes, accuracy metric, and stated BEV-LLM training settings remain unchanged. Whether the revised baseline scores reflect changed testing procedures cannot be determined.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 and Table 3 retain identical ablations on BEV-Fusion, camera views, and historical frames, including their results. No additional robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case analyses appear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The score revisions introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises results for all six open-source comparators under both frame conditions. For example, LLaVA-OV-7B total accuracy changes from 76.3 to 77.8 for multiple frames and from 70.2 to 75.8 for single frames. BEV-LLM remains at 78.7 and 76.2; commercial-model and ablation results are unchanged. This substantially revises the comparative evidence, although identical underlying evaluation conditions are not established.

T1.justification: The feature definitions and temporal-attention and fusion equations in Section 2.4 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset, benchmark, and BEV-LLM claims, including superiority in six subtasks and the 78.7% overall score. These claims are not revised alongside Table 2.

C2.justification: The explanations of spatial-reasoning difficulties, benefits of BEV representations, short-term temporal reasoning, and future generalization needs remain unchanged. No interpretation of the revised baseline scores is added.

D1.justification: Deleting the explicit zero-shot specification removes reproducibility information without supplying replacement evaluation details. The stated training stages, three-frame/1.5-second input, and GitHub release address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 55 references and the same positioning against existing driving VQA datasets and MLLMs are retained. No cited work or novelty argument is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 deletes the zero-shot sentence and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Otherwise, the prose and section organization remain essentially verbatim, with minor text reflow.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 receive cosmetic revisions to styling, sizing, and spacing while retaining their content. Table 2 adds separators above BEV-LLM rows and revises ranking emphasis. Some emphasis is incorrect: single-frame action recommendation bolds BEV-LLM's 81.4 despite LLaVA-NV-32B reporting 82.9.

improvement.justification: The visual refinements are outweighed by limited reporting regressions. Section 3.2 retains a 21.7% traffic-light advantage even though the relevant Table 2 comparison changes from 61.1 versus 50.2 to 61.1 versus 54.2. v2 also introduces incorrect ranking emphasis and removes the zero-shot specification without replacement, reducing consistency and evaluation clarity.
